title: Part Two, Chapter 12: The Death of Hun-ahpu and Xbalanque

verses.t: And now we shall tell here the memory of the death of Hun-ahpu and Xbalanque, and of the way they died.

When all the torments that were done to them had been ordered, they did not die by the punishments of those of the underworld, nor were they defeated by all the biting animals that were there in the underworld. Then they sent for two diviners, as it were seers and watchers, who were called Xulu and Pacam, who were wise men: "If the lords of the underworld ask you about our death, for they are gathered in council because we have not died and have not been defeated, and we have cast aside all their punishments, since the animals have no power over us, this is the sign of the instrument of our death: a burning stone will be the instrument of our death, at their hands. All those of the underworld have already gathered; but we shall not really die. And this that we tell you is what you must know and do. If they ask about our death, that we be cut to pieces, say what we shall tell you, and keep your heads bowed. If they say to you, 'Would it be good to throw their bones into the ravine?', say likewise, 'It would not be good, for they would rise again.' And if they say, 'Would it be good to hang them on trees?', say likewise, 'It would not be good, for you would see their faces again.' And when, the third time, they ask whether it would be good to throw their bones into the river, if it is said to you by them once more, say that that would be good, that it be done so that they die; and also that their bones be ground and made into flour, as an ear of corn is ground on the stone; that each one be ground, and then be thrown into the stream, there where the spring falls, so that they may go through all the hills, small and great. So you must say, and declare this warning of ours that we have given you." This is what Hun-ahpu and Xbalanque said, who already knew of their death. And those of the underworld made a great bonfire, like a pit in the ground, like an oven, and put in a great bed of embers. And then came the messengers who were to accompany them, the messengers of Hun-came and Vucub-came: "Let them come," they said, "and let us go with the young men; let them go and see how it is prepared. The lord says so to you, young men." This was said to them. "Very well," they said, and then they went quickly and came to the mouth of the bonfire; and there those who were playing wanted to force them: "Here, try this sweet drink of ours; four times each of us will fly over it, young men." This was said to them by Hun-came. And they said, "Do not deceive us like this. Do we not know our own death, lords? Look!" they said. And then, setting their faces opposite each other, they stretched out their arms, both of them, in the form of a cross, and went face down into the bonfire; and there both of them died. And at this those of the underworld were very glad, and whistling and shouting they said, "Now they are beaten; now they have given in." And afterwards they called Xulu and Pacam, to whom the twins had left their word, and they were asked in the same way, "Where shall their bones go?" And then they ground them and made them into flour, and went and threw them into the river. And they did not go far, but at once they sank to the bottom and were turned into two handsome young men, and they appeared again.
